History:
- Chief complaint: 3-day history of diarrhea with vomiting and subjective fever.
- Symptom details:
  - Diarrhea began watery, now very loose; frequency: “lost count,” at least 4 times today.
  - Vomiting: unable to keep down liquids or food; last episode ~2 hours before consult after attempting breakfast.
  - Abdominal pain: periumbilical, very tender to touch, crampy/intermittent, often precedes urge to defecate.
  - Fever: feels “boiling/roasting” but no temperature measured (no thermometer).
  - Urination: passing urine; last void ~1 hour before consult; color not assessed.
  - No blood in stool or urine. No rash.
- Exposures: Brother has similar symptoms; reports others at his school affected. No recent travel.
- Baseline bowel habit: once daily, normal.
- Self-care tried: Oral rehydration solution (salt-sugar mix) ~3 times/day for 2 days; not improving due to vomiting.
- Gynecologic: Last menstrual period ~2 weeks ago; not sexually active; not on contraception.
- Impact on function: Working from home due to illness.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: None reported.
- Surgical history: None reported.
- Medications:
  - Vitamin D daily (dose/route not documented).
  - Ibuprofen as needed for menstrual cramps (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - ORS taken ~3 times/day for 2 days (dose not documented).
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Social: Does not smoke; occasional alcohol (“a pint from time to time”); no illicit drugs. Lives with mother and brother. Occupation: Graphic designer.

Physical Examination:
- Setting: Telemedicine; no vitals recorded, no in-person exam.
- Reported findings: Subjective fever; frequent loose stools; active vomiting; periumbilical tenderness; urinating within the past hour.
- Relevant negatives: No rash; no visible blood in stool or urine.

Impression:
- Acute infectious gastroenteritis (likely viral given household exposure), with risk of dehydration due to persistent vomiting; bacterial cause to be ruled out.

Management Plan:
- Hydration: Continue oral rehydration salts in very small, frequent sips to improve tolerance.
- Diet: Light/bland foods only (e.g., toast, biscuits); avoid fruit, vegetables, and milk temporarily.
- Testing: Arrange urgent clinic visit for hydration assessment and stool sample collection for infectious workup.
- Safety-net: If symptoms worsen or patient feels more unwell, seek urgent evaluation in the Emergency Department. May call clinic back if condition changes.
- Logistics: Appointment to be scheduled via support line.

Patient Summary:
- Adult woman with 3 days of watery-to-loose diarrhea, vomiting preventing adequate oral intake, and subjective fever, with a sick household contact. No blood or travel history. Clinical picture suggests acute viral gastroenteritis; will assess hydration in clinic and send stool studies to exclude bacterial infection.
- Supportive care emphasized with ORS and bland diet; emergency care advised if deterioration occurs.

Key Takeaways:
- Take oral rehydration solution in tiny, frequent sips; avoid overfilling the stomach.
- Stick to bland foods; avoid fruit, vegetables, and milk until improved.
- Attend urgent clinic appointment for hydration check and stool testing; go to ED if feeling worse.

Next Steps:
- Urgent clinic assessment today for hydration status and stool sample submission.
- Continue ORS and bland diet pending evaluation.
- Further treatment (including possible specific therapy) to be guided by stool test results and clinical assessment.

  - Drug allergies not documented.
  - Medication doses/routes/frequencies largely not documented.
  - No vital signs (temperature, pulse, blood pressure) or objective hydration assessment.
  - Stool frequency quantification and appearance beyond “watery/very loose” limited.
  - Recent antibiotic use and specific food exposures not queried.
● Internal conflicts: None noted.
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; some pauses and brief inaudible/uncertain segments but clinical content sufficient.
